sections.content: How many people stayed in Stoke-on-Trent after gaining qualifications?

Stoke-on-Trent is a city in the West Midlands. Stoke-on-Trent also has a university.

Stoke-on-Trent has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Stoke-on-Trent ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 12,540 state-school pupils from Stoke-on-Trent who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,995 (24%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 3,585 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Stoke-on-Trent to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Stoke-on-Trent's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Stoke-on-Trent in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Stoke-on-Trent move to?

Of Stoke-on-Trent's graduates, 770 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 195 of those graduates (25%) were living fairly locally, in the Stoke-on-Trent travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Stoke-on-Trent's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 540 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 275 of those qualified non-graduates (51%) were living fairly locally, in the Stoke-on-Trent travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Stoke-on-Trent's GCSE cohort:

  • 495 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the North West
  • 230 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 27% of graduates and 21% of qualified non-graduates living in Stoke-on-Trent had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,990 graduates and 3,760 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Stoke-on-Trent. This is compared with the 2,995 graduates and 3,585 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 73% of the graduates had also lived in Stoke-on-Trent as GCSE pupils, while 27% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Stoke-on-Trent in 2018 to 2019, 79% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 21% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
